title: MDK12-Bench: A Multi-Discipline Benchmark for Evaluating Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the need for more robust benchmarks to evaluate the multimodal reasoning abilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The authors argue that existing benchmarks are too narrow in domain coverage, data size, structure, and reasoning depth, making it difficult to diagnose where current models succeed or fail on real-world academic tasks.

To address this, the paper introduces MDK12-Bench, a large-scale benchmark built from K-12 examination questions spanning six disciplines: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, geography, and information science. The benchmark includes 141,320 questions, both text-only and multimodal, and adds fine-grained annotations such as grade, curriculum, topic, knowledge points, difficulty labels, answer explanations, and cross-year partitions. The dataset was curated with the participation of over 20 researchers and several K-12 educators, using online exam repositories plus GPT-4o-assisted screening and human review.

The paper also proposes a dynamic evaluation framework that bootstraps text and image content to reduce contamination and test model robustness under altered question formats and visual styles. The benchmark is used to evaluate several closed- and open-source MLLMs, showing that current models still struggle with high-order multimodal reasoning and are sensitive to contextual changes and question perturbations. The results suggest that both stronger reasoning models and more resilient evaluation protocols are needed for future progress.

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: A Google multimodal large language model family used for image-text reasoning, generation, and question answering.
identified_tools.use_case: Benchmarked as one of several closed-source multimodal large language models on MDK12-Bench, including Gemini-2.0-flash-exp and Gemini-2.0-flash-thinking-exp.

findings.finding_summary: Gemini2-thinking achieved the highest overall accuracy on MDK12-mini at 59.4%, and Gemini2-flash followed at 57.2%. On the full benchmark and dynamic evaluation subsets, Gemini models showed substantial performance drops under bootstrapped textual/visual perturbations, indicating sensitivity to contextual shifts and potential contamination issues.
findings.measure: Accuracy on MDK12-Bench / MDK12-mini and accuracy change under dynamic bootstrapped evaluation
findings.sample_size: n=141,320 overall benchmark; n=14,595 MDK12-Mini; dynamic subset n=2,637 multimodal instances

findings.finding_summary: Under dynamic evaluation, Gemini2-thinking dropped from 58.1 to 41.6 on the sampled subset, a 16.5-point decrease overall. The paper reports an even larger decline on easy items for Gemini2-thinking (22.9 points), suggesting high sensitivity to altered context outside the original distribution.
findings.measure: Accuracy difference between original and dynamically bootstrapped queries
findings.effect_size: -16.5 percentage points overall; -22.9 percentage points easy subset
findings.sample_size: n=2,637 multimodal instances for dynamic evaluation

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based multimodal large language model family used for reasoning, question answering, and multimodal understanding.
identified_tools.use_case: Benchmarked as GPT-4o, GPT-o1-mini, and GPT-o3-mini on MDK12-Bench; also used GPT-4o API and GPT-based judging/interpreter steps in data processing and evaluation.

findings.finding_summary: GPT-4o reached 50.0% overall accuracy on MDK12-mini, while GPT-o1-mini reached 53.1%. The paper also reports GPT-4o at 51.2% on the original sampled subset before dynamic augmentation. Overall, OpenAI models performed below the best Gemini model and were challenged by dynamic bootstrapping.
findings.measure: Accuracy on MDK12-Bench / MDK12-mini and accuracy under dynamic bootstrapping

findings.finding_summary: GPT-4o dropped from 51.2 to 40.9 on the original versus dynamically bootstrapped subset, a 10.3-point decrease. The paper interprets this as evidence that the model is vulnerable to combined textual and visual perturbations and relies heavily on contextual reasoning.
findings.measure: Accuracy difference between original and dynamically bootstrapped queries
findings.sample_size: n=2,637 multimodal instances for dynamic evaluation

identified_tools.name: Claude
identified_tools.description: Anthropic's Claude model family, a general-purpose multimodal large language model used for reasoning and text-image understanding.
identified_tools.use_case: Benchmarked on MDK12-Bench as Claude-3.7-Sonnet among the closed-source MLLMs.

findings.finding_summary: Claude-3.7 scored 49.8% overall accuracy on MDK12-mini and 46.7% on the sampled original subset. It was outperformed by Gemini models and showed lower performance than the strongest open-source reasoning-oriented models in some settings.

On dynamic evaluation, Claude-3.7 dropped from 46.7 to 31.4 overall, a 15.3-point decrease. The paper uses this as evidence that the model is sensitive to combined textual and visual bootstrapping and contextual shifts.
findings.measure: Accuracy difference between original and dynamically bootstrapped queries
findings.sample_size: n=2,637 multimodal instances for dynamic evaluation

identified_tools.name: Qwen
identified_tools.description: Alibaba's Qwen multimodal model family used for vision-language reasoning and question answering.
identified_tools.use_case: Benchmarked in multiple variants, including Qwen2.5-VL-72B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen2-VL-7B, and Qwen2-VL-7B-GRPO.

findings.finding_summary: Qwen2.5-VL-72B achieved 51.9% overall accuracy on MDK12-mini, while smaller Qwen variants scored lower (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-7B at 47.9%, Qwen2-VL-7B at 43.8%, and Qwen2-VL-7B-GRPO at 44.1%). The paper concludes that larger models generally perform better, but all Qwen variants remained sensitive to subject and difficulty variation.

Under dynamic evaluation, Qwen2-VL-7B-GRPO dropped from 28.2 to 26.0 overall, and Qwen2-VL-7B dropped from 27.3 to 26.1 overall. The paper also notes that Qwen2-VL-7B showed only a small decline on the hard subset but was still vulnerable to text-format changes and contextual perturbations.
findings.measure: Accuracy difference between original and dynamically bootstrapped queries
findings.sample_size: n=2,637 multimodal instances for dynamic evaluation

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: Meta's LLaMA family of open-weight large language models.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned in related work as part of the broader LLM foundation-model landscape, but not evaluated on MDK12-Bench.

identified_tools.name: DeepSeek
identified_tools.description: DeepSeek family of reasoning-oriented large language models.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned in related work as a reasoning model family (DeepSeek-R1 / DeepSeek-E1 style reasoning) and not evaluated directly in the benchmark results presented here.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / multimodal large language models used for reasoning, text interpretation, and answer generation when no single product is the focus.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper broadly evaluates multiple multimodal large language models as benchmark subjects and uses GPT-based tools for automatic screening, parsing, translation, and answer judging.

findings.finding_summary: Across the benchmark, current MLLMs showed significant limitations in multimodal reasoning, with scores varying widely by discipline and difficulty. The paper emphasizes that more reasoning-trained models performed better, but all systems remained vulnerable to dynamic perturbations and contextual changes.
findings.measure: Benchmark accuracy across six K-12 disciplines and three difficulty levels

findings.finding_summary: The dynamic evaluation framework revealed that combined textual and visual bootstrapping substantially reduced accuracy, especially for easier tasks. The authors interpret this as evidence that MLLMs are highly sensitive to format shifts, text wording changes, and image-style transformations, raising concerns about robustness and contamination in evaluation.
findings.measure: Accuracy under bootstrapped text and image transformations
findings.sample_size: n=2,637 multimodal instances for dynamic evaluation

quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark paper rather than a K-12 intervention study, RCT, or meta-analysis. It reports empirical model evaluations, but not educational effectiveness evidence in classrooms.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports clear benchmark performance differences and sensitivity to perturbations, but effect sizes are mostly in percentage-point accuracy changes rather than standardized educational impact metrics. The findings are informative for model robustness, though classroom impact is indirect.
